name: Partial Deletion of Chromosome X Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Chromosome X Partial Deletion Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Identification of partial deletion on the X chromosome by cytogenetic or molecular genetic testing
Presence of characteristic clinical features including short stature, gonadal dysgenesis, and skeletal anomalies
Exclusion of other chromosomal abnormalities or syndromes with overlapping features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation of partial X chromosome deletion plus presence of at least two major clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic testing combined with clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic underdevelopment or absence of functional ovaries
Abnormal outward angulation of the forearm

common.notes: Failure to initiate or complete puberty
Skin folds extending from the neck to the shoulders

common.symptomName: Cardiac malformations, especially bicuspid aortic valve

occasional.symptomName: Hearing loss due to recurrent otitis media
occasional.notes: Conductive hearing impairment secondary to infections
searchTerms: hearing problems due to otitis media

rare.notes: Rare association with autoimmune thyroiditis or other conditions
Mild to moderate intellectual disability in some cases

laboratory: Elevated gonadotropins (FSH, LH) indicating gonadal failure
imaging: Ultrasound showing streak ovaries or absent gonadal tissue
Echocardiogram revealing bicuspid aortic valve or other cardiac anomalies
Skeletal X-rays demonstrating cubitus valgus and other bone abnormalities
genetic: Detection of partial deletion on the X chromosome by karyotyping or microarray
Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) confirming deletion region
other: Physical examination revealing webbed neck and lymphedema
Audiological testing confirming conductive hearing loss

distinguishingFeatures: Complete or partial monosomy X rather than partial deletion
Characteristic phenotypic features including shield chest and widely spaced nipples
More frequent cardiovascular anomalies such as coarctation of the aorta
Presence of extra X chromosome (47,XXY) rather than deletion
Male phenotype with hypogonadism and tall stature

redFlags: Severe short stature with skeletal deformities
Congenital heart defects detected in infancy
references: Orphanet: Partial Deletion of Chromosome X Syndrome - ORPHA:263726
